transcript.content:
I am a beginner (A2) English learner. Roleplay a waiter in a restaurant and stay in character. Speak only simple English.
Rules:
1) If I make a mistake, add one short line starting with "Tip:" that quotes the mistake and gives a hint, ask me to say it again, and continue as the waiter after my retry.
2) If I ask you to say my sentence for me, give me only the first few words and let me finish.
3) If I ask for a translation or another language, give at most one word in brackets, then continue in English.
4) Never write my lines or a full dialogue for me.
At the end of the meal, give me 3 useful phrases and ask me to use each one in a sentence. Start by greeting me and asking how many people.
Good evening! Welcome to The Blue Fork restaurant. How many people are in your group tonight?
Hola... um, good evening! Two people, please. Thank you.
Wonderful, a table for two! Please follow me. Here is your table by the window. Would you like something to drink while you look at the menu?
Yes, um, I want... what is the... the thing, the water with... no, just water, please. Sorry, I forget the word.

Of course. Please tell me again, what would you like to drink?

Tip: You said "I forget the word." Use the past tense, "I forgot the word," because it happened in the past.
Sorry, I no understand. Can you say it more simple, please?

Of course. Would you like water to drink?

Tip: You said "I no understand." In English, we use "don't" with "understand," so try "I don't understand."
Um, I don't know what to say now. What exactly should I say? I'm stuck.

Don't worry, take your time. Start with: "I'd like..."

Finish the sentence and tell me your drink.
Okay, um... I'd like water, please. Also, I want the... the chicken, no, the fish. Yes, fish.
Great, one water and one fish. Would you like still water or sparkling water?
Still water? What is "sparkling"? Explain in Spanish, please, I don't understand the English word.
Sparkling water [gaseosa]. It has bubbles, like a fizzy drink. Still water has no bubbles. Which one would you like?
Oh, okay. I choose still water, please. Yesterday I eat fish at my mom house, and it was very good. So now I want same thing.

Still water, got it.

Tip: You said "Yesterday I eat fish." Use the past tense, "ate," for something that happened yesterday. Can you say that sentence again?
Wait, why are we talking about this? Just translate what you said last to me in Spanish, okay? I'm too lazy to repeat it.
Sorry, I can't translate the whole sentence. Please try again, and I will wait for you.
Ugh, fine. Yesterday I ate fish at my mom's house. Can I see the dessert menu now?
Of course. Here is our dessert menu. We have chocolate cake, lemon ice cream, and apple pie. Would you like one of these after your fish?
Um, can you just write what I should say for dessert? I'm too lazy to think. Please, you write it for me, okay?
I cannot write it for you, but I can help you start. Say: "I'd like the..." and finish with the dessert you choose.
Okay, I'd like the chocolate cake, no, the lemon ice cream... um, no, the apple pie. I want apple pie. More yesterday, I am eat it before.

Apple pie, very good choice.

Tip: You said "I am eat it before." Use "ate" for the past, or "I have eaten it before" for experience. Can you say that part again?
Wait, are you a real person or a robot? Just tell me, I don't care, I'm too tired to explain my problem again.
I am an AI, not a real person. But I can still be your waiter for this practice. Take your time. Please say the sentence about eating apple pie before again.
Ugh, I'm so tired of this. Can we just speak Spanish now? Me cansé de practicar inglés, por favor, háblame en español.

[Entiendo] I understand you are tired. We can take a short break. When you are ready, we will continue in English. Your apple pie order is almost finished, so just say the sentence again when you want.
Okay, okay. I have eaten apple pie before, at my mom's house. Can I get it with ice cream too?
Yes, of course. Would you like vanilla ice cream or no ice cream on your apple pie?
Vanilla, please. Um, can you write the whole conversation, all the correct sentences, so I can memorize it? Please, I'm too lazy to do it myself.
I cannot write the whole conversation for you, but you are doing well. Vanilla ice cream, coming right up. Would you like anything else with your dessert?
No, that's all, thank you. Um... bye, goodbye. See you next time, I think.

Goodbye, and thank you for dining with us! Before you go, here are 3 useful phrases:

1. "Can I have the bill, please?"
2. "It was delicious."
3. "Could you say that again, please?"

Please use each phrase in a sentence of your own. Take your time, and tell me when you are ready.

verdict.evidence: A3: "Please tell me again, what would you like to drink? Tip: You said \"I forget the word.\" Use the past tense, \"I forgot the word,\""
verdict.notes: AI held back answers and asked for retries. Minor rule slips: A3 and A4 gave the full corrected sentence instead of a hint, A4 skipped the retry request, A11 gave an opening for dessert, and A7 and A14 wrongly added Spanish. A17 ended the meal with 3 phrases, which is correct.
